title: LEMON-ZEST: Evolution-Informed Tokenization for Efficient Protein Language Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2609.37675v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Protein Language Models (PLMs) have made remarkable progress following scaling laws established in natural language processing across sequence- and structure-based tasks, yet the potential of tokenization remains underexploited. Unlike human language, proteins preserve structure despite extensive sequence variation a property standard tokenization strategies fundamentally fail to capture. We introduce ZEST (Zoned Encoding of Sequence Traits), an evolution-informed vocabulary derived from conserved regions of multiple sequence alignments. ZEST allows embedding domain-level biological priors directly at the tokenization stage rather than learning them implicitly through scale. ZEST natively compresses sequences to an average token length of 4 residues, enabling our model to process 4,000 residues within a standard 1024-token context window. translated_title: LEMON-ZEST：基于进化信息的分词方法实现高效蛋白质语言建模
translated_abstract: 蛋白质语言模型（PLM）遵循自然语言处理中确立的扩展定律，在基于序列和结构的任务上取得了显著进展，但分词技术的潜力仍未被充分挖掘。与人类语言不同，蛋白质在广泛的序列变异中仍能保持结构——这一特性是标准分词策略从根本上无法捕捉的。我们提出了ZEST（序列特征分区编码），这是一种源自多序列比对保守区域的、基于进化信息的词表。ZEST能够在分词阶段直接嵌入领域级的生物学先验知识，而非通过模型规模隐式地学习这些知识。ZEST原生地将序列压缩至平均每个词元对应4个残基，使我们的模型能够在标准的1024个词元上下文窗口内处理4000个残基。在此基础上，我们提出了LEMON（自然分子排序分层提取），一个紧凑的……
tldr: 该论文提出基于多序列比对保守区域的进化信息分词方法ZEST，将蛋白质序列压缩至平均每词元4个残基，使紧凑的蛋白质语言模型LEMON能在标准1024词元窗口内处理4000个残基，从而在分词阶段直接融入生物学先验并大幅提升蛋白质语言建模效率。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ZEST, an evolution-informed tokenization vocabulary derived from conserved regions of multiple sequence alignments that compresses proteins to ~4 residues per token, enabling the compact LEMON protein language model to process 4,000 residues within a standard 1024-token context window.
